primitives.note: Toggle between Pow-Pow (plain autoattacks that build Rev'd up AS stacks) and Fishbones (autoattacks cost mana on-attack, deal 110% AD modified physical damage + AoE splash, gain range, lose 10% bonus AS).
Rev'd up: Pow-Pow autoattacks build up to 3 stacks of bonus attack speed (first stack twice as potent, each stack expires individually 2.5s after being granted/refreshed).

Get Excited!: a champion takedown grants up to 5 stacks of 25% total AS beyond the normal cap, decaying over 6s; only fires on a kill, which in a single-dummy damage fight happens once at the very end.
Fishbones mode adds modified physical damage (110% AD, crit-affected) to the primary target on every basic attack, plus AoE splash to nearby enemies (proc damage, no lifesteal/on-hit).
Passive raises Jinx's attack speed cap to 90.0 while stacked; Fishbones mode separately reduces her bonus attack speed by 10%.
Both normal and Fishbones-mode primary-target autoattack damage can critically strike; Fishbones AoE splash cannot.
Zap!, Flame Chompers!, and Super Mega Death Rocket! deal damage on cast/impact on their own cooldowns.
R's bonus damage scales with the target's missing health (25-35% base, 20-28% on secondary/AoE targets), independent of the travel-distance component.
Mana costs (20 per Fishbones autoattack, plus W/E/R cast costs) can meaningfully constrain casts/attacks across a 15s fight, especially sustained Fishbones autoattacking.

R's damage ramps with projectile travel distance up to 1500 units (10% to 100% of max) and its secondary AoE (80% damage) plus E's chomper splash only matter with multiple targets or engagement distance, both of which a single stationary dummy fight must assume a value for.

needsBespoke.why: Q is a toggle that swaps Jinx's entire basic-attack profile (damage formula, range, attack-speed penalty, and a per-attack mana cost rather than a per-cast cost) between two stances, and a Rev'd up stack built in one stance is only partially honored on the first attack after switching to the other. The closed primitive list can approximate the pieces (weapon-or-ammo-system, stacking-self-buff, onhit-rider, resource-budget) but none of them natively models 'cost attached to every basic attack while in a given stance' or 'buff partially carries across a stance switch for exactly one attack', so bespoke logic is needed to wire these primitives together correctly for Jinx.

proposal: Toggle Switcheroo! to Fishbones at the start of the fight for extra per-attack physical damage and range.
Fire Super Mega Death Rocket! (R) as early as feasible, positioned to maximize its travel-distance damage bonus before it hits the target.
Cast Flame Chompers! (E) and Zap! (W) on cooldown throughout the fight for their flat direct damage.
Autoattack continuously with Fishbones for its per-hit bonus damage as long as mana allows.
If mana runs low, toggle back to Pow-Pow (no cast cost) and keep autoattacking to build Rev'd up attack-speed stacks and sustain DPS without further draining mana.
Recast W and E again as their cooldowns come up (both are short enough to be used multiple times in 15s); R likely only fires once given its long cooldown relative to a 15s window.
questions: Given typical mid/late-game AD and mana pool for this build, is sustained Fishbones autoattacking (extra flat damage per hit, mana-limited) actually higher DPS over 15s than staying in Pow-Pow and stacking attack speed, or does mana starvation make Pow-Pow the stronger choice?
Should the simulator toggle Q mid-fight (Fishbones -> Pow-Pow) when mana is depleted, or does the dummy fight assume unlimited/refilled mana so Jinx should just stay in Fishbones the whole time?

Does the simulator engage the dummy at Fishbones' extended range from the start, or does Jinx begin in Pow-Pow's shorter range and switch weapons only after closing distance, delaying the first few high-value hits?
